column1: # Dispositions for verify-meaning.py, Phase 158's own sibling of _DISPOSITIONS.tsv,
# _DISPOSITIONS-batch10.tsv and _DISPOSITIONS-docs.tsv (D-13, phase 158-05). A new
# sibling file is required, not an append to either predecessor: _DISPOSITIONS-docs.tsv
# is frozen at exactly 6 data rows by a Phase 154 contract, and _DISPOSITIONS-batch10.tsv
# carries zero data rows and is Phase 156's own sibling for the batch-10 corpus. The
# loader (load_dispositions) silently accepts a row from any file regardless of which
# phase it belongs to -- nothing mechanical stops a wrong-file append -- so the
# separating ground is the phase-scoped key space, a decision, not a parser constraint.
# Neither predecessor table is touched by this file.
# BASE for this run is d0b611e8 (D-12, bare, this phase's fixed corpus-verification
# revision). At that BASE, `python scripts/docs-style/verify-meaning.py d0b611e8`
# (default --dispositions, i.e. none loaded) reports 14 undispositioned findings: 9 on
# docs/ files and 5 on .planning/ files -- MEASURED live in this plan's own execution,
# not copied from 158-CONTEXT.md's D-12 figure of "4" planning-tree findings. The fifth
# is a live divergence from that written figure: three more plans (158-01 through 158-04)
# landed ordinary planning-process commits after D-12 was measured, and the checker has
# no path scoping, so it counts every one of them. All five are attributed here, not
# given rows:
#   - .planning/REQUIREMENTS.md (label-drift): the STD-01..04 checkbox flip from
#     `[ ]` to `[x]` plus the `[SUPERSEDED 2026-09-05]` annotation block landed by
#     Phase 157's own amendment mechanism, an ordinary requirements-tracking edit.
#   - .planning/STATE.md (frontmatter): `last_updated` timestamp advances on every
#     plan-boundary commit; routine session-continuity bookkeeping.
#   - .planning/STATE.md (quotation): the ISO timestamp inside a quoted "..." span in
#     the frontmatter's own dependency-graph text moved with the same timestamp advance.
#   - .planning/WINDOWS.md (frontmatter): `open_count`/`total_count`/`last_updated`
#     advanced when plan 158-03 appended ledger entry #16; routine ledger bookkeeping.
#   - .planning/seeds/SEED-001-macos-psso-admin-setup-doc-accuracy.md (frontmatter):
#     `status: planted` -> `status: closed`, Phase 157's HYG-07 seed-closure disposition.
# None of the five is a corpus (docs/) file; all five are ordinary close-out artifacts of
# this milestone's own planning process, which the checker sees only because it has no
# path scoping to exclude .planning/. Padding this table with rows for them would make
# the table's own row count meaningless and would hide that the corpus criterion (zero
# undispositioned docs/ findings) is already met without them. The literal process exit
# of `verify-meaning.py d0b611e8 --dispositions scripts/docs-style/_DISPOSITIONS-158.tsv`
# therefore remains 1 (non-zero) even after this file dispositions all 9 docs/ findings,
# exactly as a predecessor phase (156, batch-10) recorded for its own analogous 4-finding
# planning-tree residue. This is a known, logged limitation of a checker with no path
# scoping -- not a failure of this table, whose own criterion is "zero undispositioned
# docs/ findings", a claim proven below, independent of the tool's literal exit code.
# The 9 docs/ findings are all `htmlcomment` (an HTML comment changed inside a
# `<!-- ... -->` block; ABAUDIT-NN comments carry validator waivers so a restyled one
# can silently break a suppression). Eight of the nine share one root cause -- the
# wiring-comment class -- and the ninth shares the finding TYPE but not the cause; each
# still gets its own row and its own reason rather than one row repeated nine times,
# per this phase's own instruction that a repeated reason is a class rule, not a
# disposition.
#   Wiring-comment class (8 of 9): Phase 157's D-30 STD-03 authoring instruction
#   ("Author this document's prose against the Prose Style Authoring Standard ...
#   before promoting status from Draft to Approved") was inserted into each doc-class
#   template's top-of-file HTML authoring comment, and the em-dash sweep (plan 158-03)
#   additionally tightened a spaced em dash inside the same comment block on 7 of the 8.
#   Both changes are authoring-instruction metadata inside a template's own comment,
#   never corpus prose a reader sees, and never an ABAUDIT-NN validator-waiver comment.
#   Different class (1 of 9): docs/admin-setup-android/08-cope-full-admin.md's HTML
#   comment is a citation-provenance footer, not a template wiring comment; Phase 157's
#   HYG-02 leak-class fix replaced the internal-process word "RESEARCH" with
#   "phase research" inside it (a corpus-consistency terminology correction, not a
#   restyle of the cited MS Learn source or its confidence/date fields), and the
#   em-dash sweep separately tightened one spaced dash in the same comment on a
#   different line further down the same file.
